newsitem.title: ROMANIA: RADIO ROMANIA AFTERNOON HEADLINES AT 1 PM.
newsitem.headline: RADIO ROMANIA AFTERNOON HEADLINES AT 1 PM.

text.p: * The Romanian government held on Wednesday a first round of talks with representatives of the International Monetary Fund (IMF), aimed at assessing the country's progress in compliance with the loan memorandum signed in April.

The IMF's chief negotiator for Romania, Poul Thomsen, met Prime Minister Victor Ciorbea, Finance Minister Mircea Ciumara, Reform Minister Ulm Spineanu, central bank (BNR) governor Mugur Isarescu and the president of the State Ownership Fund, Sorin Dimitriu.

* Talks are scheduled to continue until August 15 in order to allow clearance of a second tranche -- worth $86 million -- of the IMF"s $430 million loan, the government's spokesman Eugen Serbanescu said.
The next round of talks is due on Monday, he said.

* Last week Ciorbea said Romania had fulfilled all requirements for the release of the seconf d tranche, as comprised in the memorandum. He singled out slowing down of inflation and increasing BNR hard currency reserves as some of the achievements.
* Hungary reopened its consular office in the Transylvanian city of Cluj, in a ceremony attended by Romanian Foreign Minister Adrian Severin and his counterpart Laszlo Kovacs.
The two ministers hailed the move as a return to normality, after years of inter-ethnic frictions. The Hungarian consulate in Cluj was closed by Communist authorities in 1988.
* Kovacs said the opening was the highlight of his three years in office and praised Cluj inhabitants for the joy and applauds with which they welcomed the ceremony.
Not one single sign of hostility was to be seen in Cluj on Wednesday, Severin said.

* Minister Adrian Severin met the ambassadors of European Union member-countries in Romania and the head of EU's mission to express Romania's position regarding a recent European Commission report on Eastern European countries invited to start membership talks, the foreign ministry said in a statement.
It said Romania was suprised that the Commission's Agenda 2000 was discriminating against some Eastern European countries in terms of when those countries would start membership negotiations.

Severin told ambassadors that Romania would boost its efforts to comply with EU membership criteria and hoped that the union's summit in December in Luxembourg would respect the principle of equal chances and would invite Romania to start talks at the same time with its neighbours.
* Dumitru Ciausu met French president jacques Chirac to present his credentials as Romania's ambassador to paris.

Ciausu passed a friendship salute to Chirac on behalf of President Emil Constantinescu and presented "the feelings of gratitude on behalf of the Romanian people for France's efforts in supporting the Balkan country's bid for NATO and EU membership".
